result.title: MARS: Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams for Video Forgery Detection
result.summary: Generalizing deepfake detection across facial manipulation and fully generated video remains challenging due to forgery traces varying with the manipulation method and scene content. Explicit spatial and temporal feature differences offer a way to capture this variation, but also respond to natural texture and motion, motivating their joint interpretation with appearance features. We investigate whether combining multiscale feature differences with adapted appearance representations improves detection across both forgery categories. We introduce Multiscale Appearance-Residual Streams (MARS), a two-path video detector. The residual path applies fixed spatial and temporal difference-of-Gaussians operators to frozen intermediate features and models the resulting differences alongside appearance context across frames. The semantic path adapts the encoder's normalization parameters for frame classification, and a clip-dependent gate combines their predictions. Under a shared protocol across seven datasets, MARS achieves the highest average AUROC of 91.43\%, outperforming seven compared detectors. When trained on facial manipulations alone, MARS achieves 93.99\% AUROC on GenVideo and 75.50\% on DF26, demonstrating transfer to generated videos without generated-video training data. MARS also provides signed patch and frame contributions, whose faithfulness we evaluate through controlled spatial and temporal removal against random controls. MARS is publicly available for research: Project page: https://vectorinstitute.github.io/mars/ Github: https://github.com/VectorInstitute/mars

AI.brief_summary: MARS 提出双路径视频伪造检测器：一路在冻结特征上施加固定的空间与时间高斯差分算子建模残差，另一路调整编码器归一化参数做外观分类，并按片段门控融合两路预测，跨七个数据集报告平均 AUROC 91.43%。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于视频伪造检测的判别任务，虽涉及多尺度特征差与门控融合，但未研究 VLM 推理状态、证据筛选或 latent 表示的使用与训练，与 LVR 主线缺乏具体可借鉴联系。
